relationships.title: Nvidia guarantee of Nscale's Ward County, Texas facility lease
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia stands behind {counterparty}'s Texas lease for up to {contingent_max}, so it pays only after {counterparty} has already failed to pay its landlord.
relationships.definition: Under a Guarantee of Lease Agreement of 14 October 2025, Nvidia guarantees Nscale's payment obligations under a net lease of a facility in Ward County, Texas, for the first five years of the lease. In return Nscale issued Nvidia warrants over Series B preferred shares, plus default warrants that become exercisable only if Nscale defaults on the lease. Nscale holds an escrow as recourse for Nvidia.

headline.note: Nscale states up to $860,340,000 (Note 10: $860.3m); Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-10-26 states a maximum gross exposure of $860 million for one partner.

committed_total.note: A guarantee has no committed funding; the exposure is contingent.

funded.note: Nvidia states it has made no payments under its guarantees to date (CFO commentary, 2026-11-17, ev_50045).

contingent_max.trigger: Nscale fails to pay its obligations under the Ward County, Texas net lease during the first five years of the lease
contingent_max.note: Gross maximum. Recourse: $470.0m escrow held by Nscale for Nvidia (ev_40004). Net of escrow about $390m (analysis). Dated to the 2025-12-31 audited balance sheet whose notes state the $860.3 million maximum (ev_40046).

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-10-26 reports one facility lease guarantee, maximum gross exposure $860 million, given in exchange for warrants, with $470 million placed in escrow by the partner (ev_10159, ev_50074, ev_10160). Nvidia does not name the partner. Matching amount, escrow, warrant consideration and quarter identify it as Nscale (analysis). The guarantee is now one of the land, power and shell guarantees totalling $3.5 billion (ev_10123). Nvidia never names Nscale, the landlord or the site.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: Nscale's S-1/A of 2026-11-12 states Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $860,340,000 of its obligations under the Ward County lease for the first five years, against a $470.0 million escrow and Series B warrants (ev_40003, ev_40046, ev_40004, ev_40006, ev_40007). The landlord Ionic Digital's S-1/A states Nscale provided a guarantee from NVIDIA Corporation for the lease (ev_170012), a third party confirmation of existence but not Nvidia's side.

differences.nvidia_value: Escrow $470 million; partner executed an agreement to sell the data center cloud capacity
differences.counterparty_value: Escrow $470.0 million; no capacity sale agreement mentioned in the guarantee disclosure

differences.nvidia_value: Nvidia does not state the beneficiary, landlord, site or lease; the link to Nscale rests on matching amount, escrow, warrants and quarter (analysis)
differences.counterparty_value: Nscale and its landlord Ionic Digital both name NVIDIA Corporation as guarantor of the Ward County lease

credit.wwr_reason: Nvidia pays only if Nscale defaults on the lease, so the exposure turns into a payment exactly when Nscale is weakest. The default warrants then give Nvidia more Nscale equity, which is worth least at that moment.
credit.collateral: $470.0 million escrow held by Nscale as restricted cash as recourse for Nvidia during the guarantee period (ev_40004). Default warrants over Series B preferred shares exercisable on a Relevant Default Event, fair value $11.3 million at issue (ev_40007). Nvidia may also look to the warrant shares, but their value depends on Nscale.
credit.tenor: First five years of the lease; lease commencement date not disclosed.
credit.notes: Consideration: Non-Default warrants over up to 9,476,700 Series B preferred shares with aggregate value $60.0 million, exercisable from 2026-08-01 (ev_40005, ev_40006). Nscale's Default warrant valuation inputs include a 13.6% credit spread and 77.7% lease payment recovery assumption (S-1/A fair value note; not recorded as evidence). Landlord not named.

covered_project_debt.note: Commitments under the Ward County GPU Facility of August 2026 (drawn amount not disclosed). It finances GPU infrastructure at the site whose lease Nvidia guarantees; it is not the lease itself (analysis).

first_order.trigger: Nscale misses rent under the Ward County lease within the first five years
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia pays the landlord up to the guaranteed maximum and recovers first from the Nscale escrow
first_order.text: If Nscale misses rent on the Ward County lease, Nvidia pays the landlord up to the cap and recovers first from the $470.0 million Nscale escrow.

first_order.trigger: A Relevant Default Event under the guaranteed lease
first_order.mechanism: Default warrants let Nvidia take more Nscale preferred shares
first_order.text: A Nscale lease default also makes Nvidia's default warrants exercisable, turning part of a guarantee loss into a larger Nscale stake worth least at that point.

second_order.trigger: Nscale stops paying rent at Ward County
second_order.mechanism: Ward County GPU Facility lenders finance equipment in a building whose lease Nvidia guarantees
second_order.text: JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs fund GPUs in Nscale's Ward County building, so Nvidia's lease guarantee keeps their collateral housed even if Nscale stops paying rent (analysis).

second_order.trigger: Nvidia stops giving lease guarantees to early-stage clouds
second_order.mechanism: Landlords would ask Nscale and peers for larger deposits or higher rents
second_order.text: Nvidia's credit let Nscale sign a large Texas lease while it relied on financing not yet committed, so without such guarantees Nscale would need cash deposits instead.

second_order.trigger: Nscale stops paying rent to Ionic Digital
second_order.mechanism: Nvidia's guarantee covers the first five lease years of the Nscale lease Ionic Digital relies on
second_order.text: Ionic Digital, the Ward County landlord, has about $1.95 billion of contracted rent over the initial term, and Nvidia's guarantee covers the first five lease years, so Ionic's financing of the site looks to Nvidia's credit before Nscale's (analysis).

amount.note: Facility commitments shared with Goldman Sachs; individual share not disclosed.

relationships.title: Nvidia rents reserved GPU cluster capacity from Nscale (NVIDIA MSA)
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia rents reserved GPU capacity from {counterparty} for {committed_total}, giving a young cloud contracted revenue built on Nvidia's own chips.
relationships.definition: Under a master cloud services agreement of July 2025 and related order forms, Nscale provides Nvidia with reserved GPU cluster capacity at data centers in Iceland, the United Kingdom and Norway. Initial service terms range from 12 to 48 months, for an aggregate amount of $1.2 billion.

headline.note: Aggregate amount of the NVIDIA MSA and order forms. Contract value at signing (July 2025; day not disclosed, month end used); amount already delivered and paid is not disclosed.

committed_total.note: Reserved capacity under signed order forms; termination rights not disclosed. Contract value at signing (July 2025; day not disclosed, month end used); amount already delivered and paid is not disclosed.

funded.note: Amounts Nvidia has paid are not disclosed. Nscale's largest customer is unnamed (73% of FY2025 revenue, 52% of first-half 2026 revenue).

contingent_max.note: A capacity rental has no contingent payment.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: No Nvidia disclosure naming Nscale or this agreement found as of 2026-11-23. Nvidia reports multi-year cloud service agreements only in aggregate.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: Nscale's S-1/A describes the July 2025 NVIDIA MSA: reserved GPU cluster capacity in Iceland, the UK and Norway, 12 to 48 month terms, aggregate $1.2 billion (ev_40001, ev_40002).

credit.wwr_reason: Nvidia pays rent for capacity it receives; the exposure does not grow if Nscale weakens, though delivery failure would cost Nvidia capacity it may need. Both move with AI demand.
credit.collateral: None. Nvidia receives compute capacity for its payments.
credit.tenor: Initial service terms of 12 to 48 months from service start; start dates not disclosed.
credit.notes: Whether Nvidia is Nscale's unnamed largest customer is not disclosed (ev_40025, ev_40026).

first_order.trigger: Nscale fails to deliver the reserved clusters in Iceland, the UK or Norway
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia loses reserved capacity and must rent elsewhere
first_order.text: If Nscale cannot deliver the reserved clusters, Nvidia must find capacity for its own workloads elsewhere, while Nscale loses one of its few contracted revenue lines.

second_order.trigger: Nvidia rents capacity from Nscale
second_order.mechanism: Nscale buys Nvidia GPUs through OEMs to serve customers including Nvidia
second_order.text: Nvidia's rent to Nscale helps fund Nscale's purchases of Nvidia GPUs through OEMs, so part of that hardware demand is paid for with Nvidia's own money (analysis).

second_order.trigger: The Nvidia order forms end or are not renewed
second_order.mechanism: Macquarie's Iceland facility is secured on GPU assets at a site whose capacity the NVIDIA MSA may use
second_order.text: Macquarie lends to Nscale against GPUs in Iceland, one of the Nvidia MSA locations, so the end of Nvidia's order forms would weaken that collateral's earnings (analysis).

depth2_links.description: Lender under the $331.9 million Macquarie Iceland facility; the NVIDIA MSA covers capacity in Iceland (site match is analysis).

relationships.notes: Part of Nvidia's aggregate multi-year cloud service agreements (analysis); the remainder is computed in R7.

Series C-4, 23,410,920 shares at $20.39, Series C Completion 2026-03-27

first_order.mechanism: Preferred shares absorb losses after secured lenders, lessors and noteholders
first_order.text: If Nscale cannot raise the financing it says its 2027 obligations require, Nvidia's preferred shares are paid only after secured lenders, lessors and noteholders.

events.summary: Nscale issues Series B preferred shares; Nvidia buys 63,177,840 of them for $400.0 million.
Nvidia signs the Guarantee of Lease Agreement for Nscale's Ward County, Texas facility and receives Series B warrants.
Nvidia's 10-Q reports its first facility lease guarantee, $860 million maximum, with a $470 million partner escrow, without naming the partner.
At Series C Completion Nvidia's $300 million SAFE converts into Series C-3 shares and Nvidia buys Series C-4 shares for $477.4 million.
Nvidia subscribes for $1.0 billion of Nscale convertible loan notes and agrees a further $1.0 billion NVIDIA Sale.
Nscale's S-1/A discloses the July 2025 NVIDIA MSA for reserved GPU capacity, aggregate $1.2 billion.
Nebius first appears in Nvidia's 13F with 1,190,476 Class A shares.
Nvidia and Nebius sign the securities purchase agreement and Nvidia pays $2.0 billion for a pre-funded warrant.
Nvidia files a Schedule 13G reporting 22,256,412 Nebius shares, 9.3% of Class A, including the warrant shares.
Nvidia and IREN announce a partnership; IREN grants Nvidia rights to buy up to 30 million shares at $70.
IREN's 10-K discloses the five-year Nvidia cloud services contract of about $3.4 billion.
SharonAI and Nvidia sign the Master Cloud Services Agreement and Order Form 1.
SharonAI announces the six-year Nvidia collaboration with a contract value of up to $4.88 billion.
SharonAI's 10-Q says the Nvidia arrangement has minimum revenue provisions but no fixed aggregate contractual value.
Applied Digital announces a $160 million private placement with investors including Nvidia and Related Companies.
Applied Digital first appears in Nvidia's 13F with 7,716,050 shares.
Applied Digital is absent from Nvidia's 13F for 31 December 2025; the last report showed 7,716,050 shares at 30 September 2025.
